claim: Of 496 stop-level accessibility records across 445 NYC subway station complexes in the MTA's own published dataset, 162 (32.7%) are marked ADA accessible (ada=1), 9 (1.8%) carry a second, distinct accessibility code (ada=2, undefined in-band by the source), and 325 (65.5%) are marked not ADA accessible (ada=0). At least 7 station complexes have inconsistent accessibility codes across their own constituent stops.
attributedTo: Metropolitan Transportation Authority (a New York State public-benefit authority, not a NYC city agency)

claim: The 1995 New York City Street Tree Census recorded 516,989 street tree records citywide, across a 10-value condition vocabulary (Good, Excellent, Fair, Poor, Critical, Dead, Stump, Planting Space, Shaft, Unknown). This is a raw record count, not a living-trees-only figure.
attributedTo: NYC Department of Parks & Recreation, Forestry, Horticulture & Natural Resources

claim: The 2005 New York City Street Tree Census recorded 592,372 street tree records citywide, across a 4-value status vocabulary (Excellent, Good, Poor, Dead). This is a raw record count, not a living-trees-only figure. Data-quality note: approximately 99,701 of these records carry boroname literal value "5" rather than "Staten Island".
attributedTo: NYC Department of Parks & Recreation, Forestry, Horticulture & Natural Resources

claim: The 2015 New York City Street Tree Census ("TreesCount!", run with NYC Parks staff and trained volunteer stewards) recorded 683,788 street tree records citywide, across a 3-value status vocabulary (Alive, Dead, Stump); 652,173 of those records are status=Alive. This is the most recent completed citywide census and, as of this fixture, the current governed value for this claim.
attributedTo: NYC Department of Parks & Recreation, Forestry, Horticulture & Natural Resources

claim: Of 683,788 tree records in the 2015 NYC Street Tree Census, 217,518 (31.8%) were recorded by trained community volunteers rather than paid city or census staff. Separately, of the census's living trees, 164,350 show visible signs of ongoing community stewardship (mulching, watering guards, or similar care), while 487,823 show none recorded.
attributedTo: NYC Department of Parks & Recreation, Forestry, Horticulture & Natural Resources
